subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: Should memory-core implement resumable full reindexing as a validated resumable shadow generation, direct incremental writes to the live DB, or defer resume support for now?
rationale: Source inspection proves the reliability gap, but durable generation identity, incomplete-index search/status behavior, orphan cleanup policy, and any public memorySearch configuration are product/API choices rather than a strict mechanical repair.

options.title: Resumable Shadow Generation
options.body: Persist generation/checkpoint state for the shadow DB and publish only after validation, preserving the current known-good-index invariant while allowing restart resume.

options.title: Direct Incremental Live Writes
options.body: Write checkpointed progress into the live DB with explicit incomplete-generation filtering and status semantics, accepting a larger migration and config surface.

options.title: Defer Resume Support
options.body: Keep atomic full rebuild behavior and rely on cache reuse, retry, and orphan cleanup until maintainers prioritize a broader memory indexing redesign.

recommendation.title: Resumable Shadow Generation
recommendation.body: Persist generation/checkpoint state for the shadow DB and publish only after validation, preserving the current known-good-index invariant while allowing restart resume.

likelyOwner.reason: The previous issue discussion and historical atomic reindex lineage make steipete the best available owner for the product-shape decision, with vincentkoc likely owning implementation details.
